title: Hedged warmup window + KV-rebalance scheduler tuning to reduce p99 during bursty workloads
author: Connor Alvarez
release_notes: Reduced tail latency for bursty traffic by introducing a hedged warmup window and proactive KV cache rebalancing; recommended rollout to Dedicated clusters first.
description: Context: We see periodic p99 spikes when small, latency-sensitive requests interleave with large KV-heavy requests in the continuous batcher. The root causes are (1) head-of-line short-request blocking while workers ramp kernel contexts and perform cold KV pins, and (2) long-lived KV pin hot-spots that cause repeated queue starvation on specific worker shards. This PR introduces two complementary scheduler-level mitigations: a hedged warmup window for short requests and a light-weight KV rebalancer that reduces hot-spot pinning. Goals: (a) reduce p99 and p999 tail during bursty mixed workloads, (b) preserve throughput for large KV workloads, (c) avoid added memory pressure or long GC pauses on the runtime. What this PR does (summary): 1) Hedged warmup window: add a short hedging path for requests with predicted short sequence lengths (< 128 tokens) where the scheduler can speculatively dispatch a second probe to a warmed worker if the primary queue wait exceeds a jittered warmup threshold. This hedging is rate-limited per-worker to avoid amplification and uses metrics-driven backoff. 2) KV rebalancer: implement a soft rebalancer that periodically scans KV pin distributions (approximate counts, not exact locks) and suggests lightweight pin migrations across worker shards during low-utilization windows. Migration is cooperative and bounded by a slot quota so it won't thrash hot paths. 3) Queue aging hooks: add tenant-aware age scoring to the continuous queue to bias against starvation of rarely-seen tenants; tenants with sustained wait-time increase get temporary soft-priority boosts. 4) Kernel hinting for short sequences: scheduler now emits a kernel execution hint that prefers low-latency kernels for sequences under 64 tokens on supported GPUs; this avoids costly kernel selection jitter on the hot path. 5) Telemetry and safe defaults: new SLO metrics (hedge_attempts, hedge_successes, kv_migrations, tenant_age_boosts) plus feature gates and runtime knobs for rollout. Implementation notes: - Hedged warmup is implemented at scheduler/arrival.go and worker/probe_manager.go. The hedging threshold uses a jittered value based on per-worker cold-start latency histograms. - KV rebalancer is a soft background task in worker/kv_rebalancer.go. It uses an epoch-based sample of pin counts to avoid global coordination and employs a migration token bucket. - Queue aging uses tenant token buckets and a decayed age accumulator stored in scheduling metadata; no change to request payloads. - Kernel hint plumbing touches runtime/kernel_selector.go and adds a lightweight hint struct on the dispatch path. Tests and Benchmarks: - Unit tests for hedging logic, token bucket behavior, and rebalancer quota enforcement (tests/scheduler/*). - Integration benchmark harness added to perf/bench/hedge_kv_burst.sh to reproduce characteristic workload (mix of 90% short chat-like requests and 10% long KV-annotated requests). Results: on internal perf cluster (g4dn-equivalent), relative to main at time of branch: - aggregate throughput unchanged (+1.8%) - p50 unchanged - p95 improved by ~4% - p99 improved by ~7% - p999 improved by ~12% - small increase in memory churn during targeted migration windows (+3%) Rollout plan: staged rollout via feature gate: toggle off by default; enable on dedicated clusters for 1 week with telemetry, then progressively enable for hosted low-risk customers. If p99 regressions observed, we can disable hedging or reduce hedge rate quickly via runtime flag. Risk considerations: hedging can amplify load if misconfigured; KV migrations are soft and bounded but could increase memory churn if migration tokens set too high. All knobs exposed as runtime flags and present in Redwood Console controls. Checklist: - [x] Hedged warmup implementation - [x] KV rebalance worker - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration benchmark - [x] Telemetry and dashboards - [x] Docs: scheduler/ops.md updated with knobs and recommended rollout Notes on alternatives considered: We evaluated strict priority lanes (short-first) but that starves throughput for long KV workloads. We also prototyped global KV leader election for pin placement — that added too much coordination. The chosen approach is cooperative and low-lock.

review_comments: Maya Chen (2026-02-16): Can you add more detail on the rate-limiting to prevent hedging amplification? I want to ensure we don't double the request load under tail conditions.
Connor Alvarez (2026-02-16): Added a per-worker token bucket with refill tied to successful hedge successes metric; updated description and tests to assert max 5% additional requests due to hedging.
Ravi Patel (2026-02-17): The kv_rebalancer looks promising but we need a safety cutoff if migrations push memory past threshold. Please add a guard and alert.
Connor Alvarez (2026-02-17): Added memory guard and alert rule; rebalancer halts migrations when node memory exceeds target_utilization or when migration failures > 3 in a window.
Elena Novik (2026-02-19): Noted a flaky test in probe_manager under heavy meta load; request for a small sleep removal and deterministic token refill in tests.
Connor Alvarez (2026-02-19): Fixed test by replacing time.Sleep with controlled clock in test harness; re-ran CI.
